query: I want to become a doctor but didn't get into medical school in Canada. Should I study medicine abroad?
atoms: probability of matching to Canadian residency
total financial cost of foreign medical education
quality and accreditation of the program
personal and family cost of relocation
MCAT and academic competitiveness for reapplication
alternative paths to Canadian practice (US then transfer)
emotional and resilience cost of extended training
plausible_answers: Answer A (Reapply in Canada Default): Strengthen your Canadian medical school application and reapply — improving your MCAT, gaining clinical experience, and applying more broadly has higher expected value than the financial and career risk of most foreign medical programs.

Answer B (UK or Australia if Committed): If you're committed to studying abroad, choose an accredited UK or Australian program over Caribbean schools — their graduates have substantially higher North American residency match rates and globally recognized degrees.

Answer C (Caribbean as Last Resort Only): Consider a Caribbean school only as an absolute last resort with full understanding of the match rate risk — the financial cost of attending without matching to residency is catastrophic and affects approximately 50% of Caribbean graduates.
